"executive_summary": "This paper provides a short, self-contained proof of a refinement of the classical theorem of Kodiyalam and Cutkosky, Herzog and Trung on the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of powers of ideals. The central result is Theorem 5.3, which identifies the limit of the regularity of powers of an ideal (generated in a single degree) with the maximum of the end degree of the local cohomology of the stalks of the projection from the closure of the graph of the associated rational map to its image. This proves a conjecture of Huy Tai Ha and generalizes the result of Eisenbud and Harris for ideals primary to the graded maximal ideal in a standard graded algebra over a field. A notable corollary concerns the regularity of the saturation of powers of ideals, giving a geometric criterion for the eventual linearity of reg((It)sat), and an example in a polynomial ring in n+1 variables where any graded ideal generated by n forms of the same degree satisfies reg((It)sat) = dt + b with b >= 0. The second half of the paper compares the cohomology of the stalks and the cohomology of the fibers of a projective morphism, showing that for families of projective schemes close to being flat, the maximum of the regularities of stalks and the maximum of the regularities of fibers agree, and that the maximum regularity of stalks bounds above the one for fibers under a weaker hypothesis. These results are collected in Theorem 6.9, which covers the results obtained in [EH] and [H`a]. The work is purely theoretical, with no numerical experiments, datasets, or computational benchmarks. It introduces the notion of regularity over a scheme, generalizing the usual notion of regularity with reference to a polynomial extension of a ring, and develops the machinery of local cohomology, Tor functors, and spectral sequences to establish the comparisons. The paper is a pure mathematics contribution, and the grounded distillation reflects the absence of empirical data, code, or ethical considerations beyond standard academic practice.",

{
"title": "Powers of Ideals and the Cohomology of Stalks and Fibers of Morphisms",
"authors": "Marc Chardin",
"field_subfield": "Commutative algebra / Algebraic geometry",
"type_of_paper": "Theoretical proof paper",
"executive_summary": "This paper provides a concise, self-contained proof of a refinement of the classical theorem of Kodiyalam and Cutkosky, Herzog and Trung, which states that the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of powers of an ideal over a standard graded algebra is eventually a linear function of the exponent. The central object of study is the limit of the end degrees of the local cohomology modules of the powers of an ideal, and the paper shows that this limit exists and is at least equal to the initial degree of the module. The main contribution is a proof of a conjecture of Huy Tai Ha, which asserts that this limit equals the maximum of the end degrees of the local cohomology of the stalks of the projection from the closure of the graph of the rational map defined by the generators of the ideal to its image. This result generalizes the theorem of Eisenbud and Harris, which concerns the case of ideals primary for the graded maximal ideal in a standard graded algebra over a field. A further consequence is a new result on the regularities of powers of ideal sheaves, giving a geometric criterion for the regularity of the saturation of powers of an ideal to be eventually linear. The second half of the paper compares the cohomology of the stalks and the cohomology of the fibers of a projective morphism, showing that for families of projective schemes that are close from being flat, the maximum of the regularities of stalks and the maximum of the regularities of fibers agree, and that the maximum regularity of stalks bounds above the one for fibers under a weaker hypothesis. The paper also introduces the notion of regularity over a scheme, generalizing the usual notion of regularity with reference to a polynomial extension of a ring, and defines the fiber-regularity as the maximum over the fibers of their regularity. The results are stated for positively graded Noetherian algebras and graded ideals generated in a single degree, and the paper provides a collection of results that covers the results obtained in the works of Eisenbud and Harris and Huy Tai Ha. The work is inspired by the results of Huy Tai Ha and David Eisenbud and Joe Harris, and acknowledges the contributions of Bernd Ulrich and Joseph Oesterle. The paper is purely theoretical and does not contain any numerical experiments or computational results, and the bibliography is not provided in the supplied text.",

summary.title: Powers of Ideals and the Cohomology of Stalks and Fibers of Morphisms
summary.executive_summary: This paper provides a short, self-contained proof of a refinement of the classical result of Kodiyalam and Cutkosky, Herzog and Trung on the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of powers of ideals over standard graded algebras. The central object is the limit lim_{t→∞}(end(H^i_{A+}(I^t M)) + i − t d), which the author shows exists for every i and is at least the initial degree of M for some i. The main contribution is Theorem 5.3, which identifies this limit, for ideals generated in a single degree, as the maximum end degree of the i-th local cohomology of the stalks of the projection π from the closure of the graph of the rational map defined by the generators to its image. This proves a conjecture of Huy T`ai H`a and generalizes the result of Eisenbud and Harris for ideals primary to the graded maximal ideal in a standard graded algebra over a field. A further consequence is Corollary 1.2, giving a geometric criterion for the regularity of the saturation of powers of an ideal (equivalently, powers of ideal sheaves) to be eventually linear. The second half of the paper compares the cohomology of the stalks and the cohomology of the fibers of a projective morphism, showing that for families of projective schemes that are close to being flat, the maximum of the regularities of the stalks and the maximum of the regularities of the fibers agree, and that the maximum regularity of the stalks bounds above the one for the fibers under a weaker hypothesis. These results are stated in terms of a newly introduced notion of regularity over a scheme, generalizing the usual notion with reference to a polynomial extension of a ring. The paper is purely theoretical and contains no numerical experiments, datasets, or computational results; all statements are proved theorems, lemmas, and propositions.

claims.description: The main claim is that the limit of the regularity of powers of ideals is the maximum end degree of the local cohomology of the stalks.
The second claim is that for finite morphisms there is no difference between the regularity of stalks and the regularity of fibers.
The third claim is that for near-flat families the maximum of the regularities of stalks and the maximum of the regularities of fibers agree.
The fourth claim is that the regularity of the saturation of powers is eventually linear for ideals generated in a single degree.
The fifth claim is that the notion of regularity over a scheme is natural in this situation.
